data.narrative:
Osaro, a Series B robotics and manufacturing automation company founded by Derik Pridmore and Michael Kahane, has raised $86.8M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers (including Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, Hadrian, and Nimble Robotics) and 1 public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method uses total capital raised ($87M) as a proxy valuation baseline and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-next-stage progression, yielding $165M. The peer-median method anchors to same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables: a four-company median of $1.6B, with a range of $1.0B (Nimble Robotics, Series C) to $1.8B (Bedrock Robotics, Series B).

The two methods produce materially divergent signals. Stage progression implies $165M; peer medians imply $1.6B. The triangulated range spans $140M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $895M. The gap between methods reflects uncertainty around whether Osaro's current capital efficiency and market position justify peer valuations or warrant a discount to them. Resolution requires scrutiny of unit economics, customer concentration, and competitive positioning relative to the identified peer set.
